Level Objectives A1
At the end of the level:
1. you present yourself and ask for personal information in Arabic standard, in prepared exchanges;
2. build simple nominal and verbal sentences to the present and past, even negative;
3. read teaching texts vocabulary 100–150 words on known topics, at least 40 words per minute aloud, and
answer questions for details;
4. understand slow didactic dialogues on daily life, family, work and city;
5. write 60–80 words (message, short description, tale) with errors that do not prevent the
understanding;
6. recognize cases and use them in the structures studied;
7. recognize basic structures in the titles without vowels (iḍāfa, name and adjective, nisba).

These are internal objectives of the course, written on the model of the descriptors of the Common European Framework for Level A1. Passing the exam A1 does not amount to CEFR certification (see "Seals and Evaluation").

Conventions

Transcription. The DIN system is used 31635, the same as the Level 0: ā ī ū for long vowels, ṯ ḥ ḫ ḏ š ṣ ḍ ṭ ẓ ġ for the emphatic consonants and without Italian equivalent, ʾ for the hamza, ʿ for the ʿayn, ǧ for the ǧīm. The characters' names are transliterated (Karīm, Hudā), the Italian ones not (Luke, Mary). vowels and reading. In A1 all texts are vocally available, with case terminations. The transliteration of the tables follows the reading paused: at the end of the sentence fall short final vowels and the tanwīn ( ⁧البَيْتُ كَبِيرٌ⁩ read al-baytu kabīr ). Reading aloud, trained in both ways: paused, as you speak, and with all terminations, as the exercises on cases require. Symbols. ★ in the vocabulary indicates a high frequency word to be used actively. It indicates a space to be completed. " (Recognize) " means a form that you must understand but not yet produce. Arabic and Italian on the same line. Arabic can be read from right to left even inside an Italian sentence. When multiple Arabic words are separated only by punctuation, the layout can arrange them from right to left: read them as a single Arabic phrase.
Method

The standard week (standard rhythm, 60 minutes a day): 15 minutes of Anki, 30 lessons and exercises, 15 reading aloud, listening or writing, plus a session of 30 minutes a week with the tutor. The two-week units have a plan of 14 days in the initial card. At a light pace every week of the calendar lasts two real weeks; At an intensive pace, the extra time goes to reading and conversation, not to anticipating units. How a unit is made. Each unit has the same structure: card (code, level, objectives, prerequisites, time, plan of days), dialogue with transliteration and translation, explanation with examples, pronunciation, new vocabulary with root, gender and plural, examples in context, graduated exercises, reading, writing, listening, oral production, errors typical of italophones, flashcard, final verification and criteria to move to the next unit. The solutions are in Part IV. Exercises and solutions. Always answer in writing before looking at the solutions. In tutor mode the exercises arrive one at a time and the solution is not shown before your answer, except your request. I'm listening. The course does not contain audio recordings. Each listener has a script: ask another person to read it, or paste it into an Arabic speech synthesis app without reading it first. Vocal synthesis is useful for the rhythm and recognition of words, but it can make mistakes in vowels, endings and pronunciation of some consonants: the reference pronunciation is that of the native language tutor. Anki. The Deck A1 contains all vocabulary entries, with the drive tag. Add the cards of a unit when you start it; new cards per day: 5 at a light pace, 10 Standard, 15 Intensive. About 40 Level words 0 reappear in the vocabulary A1 with new information (genre, plural, use): in the deck A1 have the tag "anche_L"0You can suspend the corresponding level card 0.

Heading (Plan, section 6.3). Five criteria with score from 1 a 4: Accuracy, Fluidity, Understanding, Pronunciation, Register. Each test uses only the relevant criteria. The pronunciation evaluates it as a native language tutor: without tutor the oral part remains open and does not replace with a self-assessment. What does a passed exam say? The exams of the course are self-correct or correct by the tutor: they attest that you have mastered the studied program, not that you possess a certified CEFR level. The most consistent external feedback with the course is the CIMA of the Institut du monde arabe, recommended at the end of A2; dates, locations and costs must be verified at the time of registration (Plan, section 6.4; Appendix C).

Studying with the tutor
For a guided session, write "Session" followed by the unit code (e.g. "Session" A1-08() and paste the last line of the register. The session always follows the same steps:
1. short recovery of the previous unit;
2. 3–5 quick questions about what you should already know;
3. explanation of the new topic with examples;
4. exercises one at a time, with the solution only after your answer;
5. correction with cause of error and a consolidation exercise;
6. updated log line and targeted review for the following days.
From A1 also serve 1–2 sessions per week with a native speaker teacher, also online: for conversation, pronunciation and correction of written productions. Oral tests and tests are done with him.
The progress log

The Excel file delivered with the first volume contains the calendar and log: one line per week with date, drives, scores, time spent and notes on errors. It is the source of truth of your journey, independent from any memory of the platform. Always note: unit verification score, test and exam section scores, address book criteria, timed reading words per minute, percentage of dictation.
